messages:
jade: quick sync: customers hit higher tail latency when compaction kicks in on GPU nodes. compaction is async but steals bandwidth; asking whether we should expose an "alloc_sla" so tenants can choose compact aggressiveness.

omar: we probably need both telemetry and API. telemetry: compaction_duration, bytes_relocated, tenant_backpressure_events. API: alloc_sla={latency|throughput|cost|balanced} + target_compact_window_ms.

li: implementation detail: compaction currently grabs global compact_lock and walks arenas. to support per-tenant SLA we need per-tenant compaction credits + work queue that respects tenant priority. big refactor.

anya: also consider soft-reserve thresholds to avoid compaction: give tenants a configurable soft-reserve so hot-serving tenants avoid being compacted aggressively. that plus credits could reduce noisy neighbor.

omar: tradeoffs: more knobs increases UI/ops complexity. start with two modes: "conservative" (minimize compaction, higher OOM risk) and "aggressive" (compact often to reclaim). map alloc_sla to those.

jade: plan: 1) add telemetry counters for compaction events (anya), 2) implement per-tenant credit queue prototype behind feature flag (li), 3) add alloc_sla API and map to credit policy (omar), 4) run perf + tail-latency experiments, then decide if we need full per-tenant compact pipeline.

offload-bot: NOTE: perf job gpu-48g compaction-smoke scheduled, link: https://ci.redwood.internal/compaction-smoke/321

jade: thanks, filing a short RFC follow-up with checklist. tagging @li @omar @anya for quick reviews. :white_check_mark:
